item.text:
# 2B.4 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is **mostly favorable** on civilian protection and humanitarian-law restraint, but it is **indirect** because Germany was not itself conducting the military operations in question. Scholz repeatedly called for ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, and compliance with international humanitarian law in Gaza. The strongest counterweight is that he still affirmed Israel’s right to defend itself and continued arms support, so this is not a pure refusal of force.

## Accepted claim items

| Type | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Strongly favorable | **Joint Statement on Gaza** | Federal Government | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/joint-statement-from-the-leaders-of-the-united-states-argentina-austria-brazil-bulgaria-canada-colombia-denmark-france-germany-poland-portugal-romania-serbia-spain-thailand-and-the-united-kingdom-on-gaza-2290942 | Scholz joined a joint statement calling for an immediate ceasefire, unconditional hostage release, protection of civilians, humanitarian aid at scale, and adherence to international humanitarian law. It also opposed annexation and called for withdrawal of Israeli forces as part of a negotiated two-state solution. This is the clearest direct evidence for 2B.4. | 2B.4 |
| Strongly favorable | **Interview des Bundeskanzlers mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said he had warned against a Rafah ground offensive, insisted that more humanitarian aid had to reach Gaza, and said every arms delivery was carefully assessed in advance. This is direct evidence of concern for proportionality and civilian harm. | 2B.4, 2B.1 |
| Strongly favorable | **Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said Israel has the right to defend itself, but warfare must comply with international humanitarian law and humanitarian aid must reach Gaza on a large scale. He also reiterated support for a two-state solution. This is explicit IHL/civilian-protection language. | 2B.4, 2B.1, 2B.3 |
| Favorable | **Video: Anniversary of the 7 October attack** | Federal Government | 7 Oct 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/media-center/chancellor-kanzler-kompakt-2313552 | Scholz called for a ceasefire one year after the Hamas attack and described the war as a disaster for the Palestinian people. This is not battlefield conduct, but it is consistent with prioritizing civilian relief and conflict de-escalation. | 2B.4, 2B.1 |
| Mixed / borderline | **Interview des Bundeskanzlers mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz affirmed Israel’s right to defend itself and said Germany remained in close contact with Israel while continuing arms support. This is the main counterweight: it supports defense and deterrence, but it does not show Germany imposing strong public conditionality tied to proportionality. | 2B.4, 2B.1, 2B.3 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Scholz endorsed violations of civilian protection, prisoner treatment, or humanitarian law.
- I also found **no direct evidence** of German battlefield conduct in 2024 to measure proportionality or necessity in a strict operational sense, because Germany was not the principal belligerent.
- The strongest limitation is that the record is mostly **about Germany’s diplomatic and arms-policy stance toward other actors’ operations**, not about German operations themselves.

## Synthesis for 2B.4

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz did respect civilian protection and humanitarian-law concerns in 2024, at least at the level of public policy and arms-transfer review.
- **Why:** he repeatedly called for humanitarian access, hostage release, ceasefire, and IHL compliance, and warned against a Rafah offensive.
- **Main caveat:** he still supported Israel’s right to defend itself and continued military support, so the posture was not anti-force; it was a restrained, law-framed support posture.

## Search gap

- I found **very little direct evidence** on prisoner treatment beyond hostage-release demands.
- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** on German conduct in combat operations, so necessity/proportionality here is inferred from Germany’s diplomatic and arms-policy choices rather than battlefield performance.
